newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia woolgrowers to get early payments.
newsitem.headline: Australia woolgrowers to get early payments.

text.p: Australian Primary Industries Minister John Anderson said on Wednesday woolgrowers would receive A$75 million from the wool stockpile in calendar 1997, earlier than previously expected.
"Today I can tell you there will be an early access for woolgrowers with equity in the stockpile," Anderson told reporters. "Initially some A$75 million will become available throughout this year."
He said the remaining surplus from the stockpile would become available in interim payments up to the end of year 2000.

Wool growers who paid levies between 1993 and 1996 to fund debts incurred by Wool International in holding Australia's wool stockpile have an equity in the wool involved. The stockpile now stands at 1.8 million bales, down from its peak of almost five million bales in 1991.

"Due to favourable developments in the wool industry, including better-than-expected market conditions, the government has taken the step of returning growers' funds early in recognition of difficulties still being experienced by many woolgrowers," Anderson said.
"This distribution of funds will not delay the retirement of the stockpile debt."
Anderson said the Wool International Act 1993 would be changed to allow section 51 reserves to be distributed to growers who paid wool tax between July 1, 1993 and June 30, 1996, as soon as possible.

He said growers would be offered a cash return or could take up equity in a growers' investment trust in order to participate in Global Wool Ltd, the proposed joint venture between WI with Elders Australia Ltd and Wesfarmers Ltd.
The new legislation would give growers legal entitlement to future equity in the significant remaining portion of the wool stockpile, he said.

"Growers will then be able to trade their entitlement, negotiate loans against the security of theif future entitlement, or keep their entitlement until the interim and final payments are completed," Anderson said.
Under the planned changes to the act, WI will be liquidated when the stockpile is sold by December 2000.
